title: Land, people, and records
paragraphs: Recovering production depended on fields, tools, animals, water, and labor. When cultivators had fled or been killed, simply returning land to use could take time. Government records also suffered; registers and local administrative capacities could not always be restored at once. This affected the state’s understanding of the population it wished to govern.

For ordinary households, a damaged register was more than an administrative inconvenience. It could affect obligations, claims, and interactions with local officials. Rebuilding official knowledge was part of rebuilding the state, yet it could place fresh demands on people already trying to recover.
